archetype: INT magician built around a light/dark duality. Light magic fills one gauge and dark magic fills the other; filling either enters Sunfire or Eclipse, and alternating between them charges into Equilibrium, a timed state where both light and dark skills gain an extra hit, cooldowns are ignored, and the Equilibrium-only attacks become available. Play is cyclical: roughly thirty seconds inside Equilibrium, then roughly thirty seconds outside it on the normal-mode kit, repeating.

gearingNotes: WSE potential target: the class doc states an optimal of nine magic attack lines with zero boss damage and zero ignore-DEF lines, and gives its reason explicitly - Luminous already carries a large amount of ignore-DEF from its own kit, so paying potential lines for more of it is wasted. This is a genuine class-specific decision and it points the opposite way from the boss-damage-and-IED default most classes use. Single source, weak consensus. Supporting mechanical evidence from the wiki, which is independent of the doc: Light Wash grants the character ignore DEF, Arcane Pitch's passive component carries ignore DEF up to 40%, Ender and HEXA Ender each carry their own additional ignore DEF, and Harmonic Paradox and Lustrous Orb add more at HEXA levels - so the innate-IED premise is consistent with the skill tables even though only one guide draws the gearing conclusion. IED benchmarks from the class doc: roughly 75-80% as a starting target, about 92% against 300 PDR bosses, about 96% against 380 PDR bosses. CRITICAL RATE: Luminous supplies a large block of its own crit - Grandis Library's base-stats-from-skills table totals +40% crit rate from passives, which the wiki breaks down as Spell Mastery +20% at level 10 and Magic Mastery +15% at level 30, plus Apocalypse - Critical Chance adding +20% to Apocalypse specifically - so links, Legion, familiars and hyper stats have a smaller gap to close than for a class with no innate crit, and this is why hyper stat crit points become reclaimable as Legion grows. ATTACK SPEED: the class doc lays out a route to the attack speed cap that sums base attack speed with Agile Magic, Spell Mastery, a Decent Speed Infusion, an Extreme Green Potion and the inner ability line; the wiki confirms Agile Magic gives +2 and Spell Mastery +1. The practical consequence is that the inner ability attack speed line is load-bearing rather than optional unless a party member supplies the missing stage. BUFF DURATION: the class doc records that buff duration does not extend Equilibrium, the class's central timed window - which is why the two sources disagree about whether buff duration deserves an inner ability line. The doc does tie buff duration to timing Ray of Redemption against its cooldown. MODE DISCIPLINE is itself a damage stat: casting a light skill while in the dark state, or the reverse, costs 50% final damage per the class doc. NOTE 2026-09-12: this field is outside the five endgame sections in scope for the resolution pass and was left untouched. Its wiki-attributed claims were NOT re-verified and maplestorywiki.net returned 403 during that pass.
